human_semantics: The red middle strip on dark cyclic head edge2 maps exactly to red light edge2 under180; blue dark edge3 maps to blue light edge3. The identical parameter fractions on negated vertices preserve strip lengths and endpoint incidence. Reading the color strips as intrinsic edging therefore retains180 and cannot supply a different valid rotation because the full polygon mean still forces180. Unmarked tips/shoulders and nearly all shafts retain original black/gray contrast, so darker/lighter source identity remains clear. The strips are continuous strokes on actual sloped boundaries, not cuts, new points, detachable pieces or changing head direction.
difference: A01 compared actual common-boundary spatial coincidence, an invariant Z subset already at the same positions. This A02 entirely removes those shaft marks and instead pairs two distinct sloped head edges on each of the two arrows, using true180 correspondences whose undirected slopes agree. Its error hypothesis is parallel unoriented directions mistaken for zero angular change despite opposite directed heads, rather than local positional overlap. Old prescreens mentioned same-side shafts and arbitrary perpendicular edges; neither is used. This is not a recolor/width-only adjustment to the failed input.
decision: Ready for exactly2 research calls; not an approval or independent second review.
